contributions.anchor: Box B 'Contributions Received this Period' = 6790.18 on the p4 Summary Page — the PROMOTED per-period cell — equal to Schedule A's own printed 'Subtotal for this page' $6790.18 and its printed 'Total Contributions Received (Sum of all Schedule A pages in this report)' $6790.18.
contributions.detail: The 4 Schedule A rows on p2 sum to 50.00 + 50.00 + 200.00 + 6490.18 = 6,790.18 exactly = the printed page subtotal = the printed sum-of-all-pages total = Box B. Single schedule sheet, so both footers share a scope; both were read rather than trusted on their captions (ADDENDUM N3 screen — neither carries a different-scope figure). Box C 'Contributions Received Year to Date' also prints 6790.18, which is consistent because this is the cycle's first and only report, but it is CUMULATIVE and was NOT used as the gate and is never summed as an increment. THE CANDIDATE'S OWN 6,490.18 IS A CONTRIBUTION ROW BY THE LADDER (ADDENDUM B3): Box A 'Balance at Beginning' prints 0, so there is no beginning-balance slot for it, and without it the rows total 300.00 against a stated 6,790.18; with it they close to the cent. It is not worded as a loan and no loan line appears anywhere on the filing.
contributions.cross_checks: Box F 'Subtotal before Expenditures (Box A + Box B)' prints 6790.18 = 0 + 6790.18, and the unlettered 'Balance at Close (Box F - Box D)' prints 0 = 6790.18 - 6790.18. The filer's ladder is internally consistent and corroborates both promoted anchors.

expenditures.anchor: Box D 'Expenditures Made this Period' = 6790.18 on the p4 Summary Page — the PROMOTED per-period cell — equal to Schedule B's own printed 'Subtotal for this page' $6790.18 and its printed 'Total Expenditures Made (Sum of all Schedule B pages in this report)' $6790.18.
expenditures.detail: The 14 Schedule B rows on p3 sum to 848.28 + 236.83 + 123.55 + 307.63 + 70.89 + 250.00 + 1363.15 + 1363.15 + 62.98 + 1162.80 + 212.82 + 54.46 + 112.48 + 621.16 = 6,790.18 exactly = the printed page subtotal = the printed sum-of-all-pages total = Box D. Box E 'Expenditures Made Year to Date' also prints 6790.18 (first and only report of the cycle) and is CUMULATIVE — not used as a gate, never summed as an increment. Rows 7 and 8 print the IDENTICAL amount 1363.15 to the same vendor on different dates (4/2 and 4/9); both were crop-checked and both exist — two real transactions, not a duplicate, and merging them would break the closure.
expenditures.cross_checks: Because Box A = 0 and the close box = 0, the filing's contributions and expenditures are identical by construction, and both sides independently close on the same figure from two different schedules — 4 rows on one and 14 on the other. That is two independent reconciliations, not one.

itemized.in_kind_convention: monetary-only closes both sides exactly. BOTH conventions were tested per ADDENDUM G1/O4 (per REPORT): this 2026 printing's Schedule A is Date / Name of Contributor / City and Zip Code / Amount with NO in-kind checkbox and NO in-kind column, Schedule B is Date / Provider/Vendor / Purpose / Amount, no row is annotated in-kind or as a donated good or service, and no amount is entered on both schedules (the two 1363.15 rows are both expenditures, and no contribution matches an expenditure by amount+date), so monetary-only and monetary-plus-in-kind give identical sums and both close at 6,790.18. in_kind=false throughout is a reading, not a default.
itemized.escalation_note: Eight tight-crop escalations at 900 dpi, none of which changed a figure. p2 (four entries, so EVERY row was proved plus a control): row 1 rendered '50', row 2 rendered '50', row 3 rendered '200', row 4 rendered '6490.18', and the row-5 control rendered an EMPTY boxed cell. Rows 2 and 3 additionally served as the proof that the two INTERPOLATED rules on p2 are real (see the p2 measure_note) — each crop shows one complete cell bounded by its own top and bottom rule, not a merged or straddling band. p3: row 1 rendered '848.28', row 14 rendered '621.16', and the row-15 control rendered an EMPTY boxed cell. No cell on this filing was doubtful: it is a born-digital fillable form, printed and re-scanned as a greyscale photocopy, so every figure is machine type rather than handwriting.
